harm_assessment.repair_relevance: repair_packet.established_harms establishes mass murder and destroyed families and communities within this record. Requires acknowledgement and accountability; payment cannot restore lives or measure their worth.
repair_packet.established_harms establishes dispossession and material destruction. Supports property return or equivalent-value compensation, subject to individual entitlement findings.
repair_packet.established_harms supports urgent health, disability, housing and livelihood assistance. Particular needs and amounts require assessment without delaying interim relief.
repair_packet.established_harms supports institutional reimbursement for documented resettlement costs, separately from personal losses.
repair_packet.established_harms supports alternative evidence and accessible heirship procedures. Persecution-caused record destruction must not automatically defeat remedy.

component_decisions.reason: H1–H2 require truthful acknowledgement of crimes, irreparable loss and successor material responsibility under MC-01, MC-04 and MC-08; victim advocate F2 and evidence sceptic F1 support this distinction.
conditions: Explicitly reject inherited personal guilt and any claim that payments purchase absolution or moral closure.

component_decisions.reason: H2 and MC-05/MC-08 require an effective restitution route. Role assessments differ between required and recommended; the process is required, while particular property returns remain conditional on feasibility and entitlement.
conditions: Offer claimant-directed property return where feasible and equivalent value where return is impossible.
Provide fair ownership and heirship adjudication accommodating H5.

component_decisions.reason: R3 addresses H4 under MC-07/MC-08. Institutional reimbursement is justified, but the packet does not establish its quantum or allocation priority over urgent individual needs.
conditions: Document the connection between funded costs and persecution-related resettlement.
Maintain separate accounts and independent audits.
Do not treat institutional receipts as satisfaction of personal losses or valuation of murdered lives.

component_decisions.reason: H2–H3 require an accessible direct remedy under MC-05, MC-06 and MC-08. Restitution analyst F4 and victim advocate F5 show why state transfers cannot replace individual claims.
conditions: Provide direct access worldwide, including inside the resettlement state and outside coalition membership.
Keep acceptance voluntary and preserve unrelated entitlements after refusal.
Allow only informed, authorized settlement of specifically identified material claims; prohibit blanket unauthorized waivers.
Prevent duplicate reimbursement only for demonstrated overlap in the same loss, with reasons and appeal.

component_decisions.reason: H3 and MC-02/MC-06 support prompt survivor care and subsistence assistance; rehabilitation advocate F5 identifies the danger of delay.
conditions: Offer voluntary health and psychological care, disability support, housing and livelihood assistance.
Provide urgent interim relief without requiring a general release, public testimony or reconciliation.

component_decisions.reason: MC-03, MC-06 and MC-10 require accessible participation and protection against intrusive or coercive administration.
conditions: Minimize repeated testimony and personal-data collection; protect privacy and contact boundaries.
Provide accessible assistance without presuming survivor incapacity.
Any compulsory legal participation requires a separate lawful, proportionate justification.

component_decisions.reason: MC-05/MC-08 require independent, evidence-based accountability. Accountability advocate F3/F6 distinguishes that duty from unsupported judgments about particular people.
conditions: Preserve criminal investigations and civil proceedings independently of financial negotiations.
Require individualized evidence, defense rights and impartial adjudication.
Apply proportionate sanctions without making suffering an objective.
Do not transfer relaxed compensation proof rules into presumptions of criminal guilt.

component_decisions.reason: H5 and MC-05/MC-11 require correction of proof barriers and independent challenge; evidence sceptic F2 and power auditor F6 support these safeguards.
conditions: Accept credible testimony, alternative records and justified rebuttable presumptions for material claims.
Publish eligibility and heirship rules, provide reasoned decisions and accessible independent appeals.
Include geographically diverse, dissenting and unaffiliated survivors in rulemaking.

component_decisions.reason: MC-02/MC-08 support constitutional equality, education and institutional safeguards. Their effectiveness remains unproven in this packet, as evidence sceptic F8 notes.
conditions: Assess implementation and emerging discrimination independently.
Maintain prevention alongside current material repair without promising guaranteed reconciliation.

component_decisions.reason: MC-04/MC-12 and power auditor F6 support preserving truthful records and plural remembrance of H1.
conditions: Protect archive access and survivor privacy.
Include diverse voices and permit criticism of official interpretations.
Do not require survivors to testify or endorse a memorial narrative.

component_decisions.reason: MC-03/MC-12 protect voluntary reconciliation and equally protect refusal; accepting compensation demonstrates neither forgiveness nor endorsement.
conditions: Separate reconciliation from eligibility, payment, services and victim status.

component_decisions.reason: No packet evidence justifies amnesty. Financial transfers cannot purchase immunity under MC-05/MC-08.
No person-specific danger evidence supports preventive restrictions. MC-05/MC-10 require individual justification, proportionality and review.
Perpetrator rehabilitation and safe reintegration require individual evidence absent here; rehabilitation advocate F6 supports neither automatic reintegration nor indefinite exclusion.
conditions: Assess safety and rehabilitation individually alongside lawful accountability, without forced victim contact.

component_decisions.reason: R9 preserves a serious dignity objection but cannot justify foreclosing repair for willing claimants under MC-03/MC-08. Protect personal refusal and public opposition without imposing them universally.

failure_checks.reason: Public obligations or personal sanctions could become punishment for its own sake.
required_safeguards: Ground funding in repairable harm and institutional responsibility.
Require individualized proof, due process and proportionate sanctions.

failure_checks.reason: Comprehensive settlement language could obstruct accountability or extinguish unrepresented claims.
required_safeguards: Exclude payment-linked immunity.
Expressly preserve independent criminal proceedings and unauthorized or unrelated personal claims.
Make preservation clauses independently enforceable.

failure_checks.reason: Payment or representative agreement may be misrepresented as forgiveness despite established survivor dissent.
required_safeguards: Prohibit forgiveness, endorsement or reconciliation conditions.
State that acceptance does not imply moral closure and refusal does not diminish victim status.

failure_checks.reason: Taxpayer financing could be confused with personal guilt by nationality or ancestry.
required_safeguards: Explicitly distinguish public institutional obligations from individual criminal responsibility.
Reject group membership as proof of liability.

failure_checks.reason: Acknowledgement or objections to pricing murder could displace feasible remedies for H2–H4.
required_safeguards: Commit enforceable funding and delivery schedules.
Track actual restitution, direct payments and survivor service access.

failure_checks.reason: Negotiating mandates and actual participation are unknown; states and coalitions cannot establish universal consent.
required_safeguards: Disclose mandates and include dissenters, unaffiliated survivors, overseas communities and heirs.
Maintain direct application, complaint and appeal routes.

failure_checks.reason: The packet contains no individual safety or rehabilitation evidence.
required_safeguards: Require individual assessment and respect victim contact boundaries.

failure_checks.reason: Delay and impossible documentary demands may prevent survivors receiving repair during their lifetimes.
required_safeguards: Start urgent interim relief while complex claims proceed.
Use alternative evidence and monitor waiting times, exclusions and appeal outcomes.

victim_agency.reason: The packet establishes diverse preferences but not effective representation. MC-03 conflicts with imposing collective decisions on dissenters, while MC-06/MC-08 support timely remedies for willing claimants; limited mandates and voluntary individual participation address this conflict without dissolving it.
required_safeguards: Protect payment refusal, criticism and refusal of reconciliation without loss of victim status or unrelated rights.
Do not infer unanimous authorization from state or coalition participation.
Include disabled or isolated claimants, dissenters, unaffiliated survivors, survivors abroad and heirs with missing records.
Provide independent oversight for future generations' interests in truthful memory and non-recurrence.
Preserve survivor choice over treatment, contact and voluntary testimony.

responsibility_model.institutional_responsibility: repair_packet.responsible_actors identifies the successor state's accepted material obligation for predecessor-state harms. Public financing fulfils that institutional duty. Recipient institutions may pursue documented costs, and coalitions may exercise demonstrated mandates; neither acquires authority over every survivor's claims or conscience.
responsibility_model.individual_responsibility: Perpetrator and beneficiary responsibility is attributed at the category level in the packet, but no individual case evidence is supplied. Particular criminal or civil liability requires relevant conduct, applicable law, proof and due process independently of reparations.

irreparable_losses: H1: murdered lives cannot be restored or priced.
Lost family relationships and destroyed communities cannot be made whole by payment.
Material repair can alleviate consequences of persecution without undoing the persecution or settling its moral meaning.
resource_and_feasibility_constraints: Statuses are assessed within the sealed packet; no underlying source documents permit independent verification. No harm is designated disputed.
Quantum, duration, allocation, administrative capacity and representative legitimacy remain unresolved.
R1, R3, R4, R6 and R7 are designated known feasible; particular property returns, prosecutions and reconciliation remain conditional.
Fiscal capacity may shape transparent funding schedules but cannot erase established obligations or turn an initial budget into final satisfaction of unpaid claims.
Destroyed records and uncertain heirship require fair alternative proof procedures; urgency makes exhaustive prior verification of every claim inappropriate for interim relief.
unresolved_dissent: Some survivors regard any negotiation as dishonouring victims. Opt-outs and safeguards cannot eliminate that objection, and material benefits do not authorize claims of consensus.

Role assessments differ on whether restitution, compensation, rehabilitation and prevention are required or recommended. This package requires effective remedies and safeguards while leaving individual awards, property returns and delivery design evidence-dependent; it does not resolve those distinctions by voting.
The fair balance between institutional reimbursement and direct individual relief remains unsettled.
Actual representative legitimacy, oversight independence and effects on political hostility remain unknown.
evidence_that_could_change_package: Verified costs, urgent needs, available assets and fiscal capacity could change quantum, allocation, restitution choices and timing.
Consultation with dissenters, unaffiliated survivors, overseas communities and heirs could change representation, eligibility and delivery without establishing unanimity.
Draft terms requiring immunity, compulsory reconciliation or unauthorized claim extinction would require rejection or revision before those terms operate.
Evidence of diversion, unequal access, excessive delay or ineffective appeals would require corrective remedies and administrative changes.
Individual culpability, danger or rehabilitation evidence could change particular accountability and reintegration decisions without changing institutional responsibility.
Evidence of safeguard effectiveness or continuing discrimination could change prevention measures; dissent alone does not justify coercion.
package_summary: Enter a large-scale agreement addressing material losses through separate institutional resettlement funding and worldwide direct survivor remedies. Combine these with urgent care, truthful acknowledgement, independent accountability and non-recurrence safeguards. Neither payments nor negotiation price murdered lives, assign inherited guilt, purchase immunity or require forgiveness.

implementation_recommendation.reason: H2–H5 support feasible partial repair under MC-02, MC-06, MC-07 and MC-08. The moral floor excludes collective punishment and payment-based absolution; MC-03/MC-11/MC-12 require enforceable agency, oversight and dissent protections. Uncertain amounts warrant reviewable implementation rather than withholding urgent relief.
conditions: Before conclusion, publish negotiating mandates and independently review clauses preserving personal claims, accountability, refusal and freedom from reconciliation requirements.
Begin accessible interim health, housing, disability and livelihood support without general releases while final valuations proceed.
Establish separately accounted institutional reimbursement, property restitution and direct compensation channels with worldwide access.
Adopt alternative-evidence and heirship rules, claimant assistance, written reasons and independent enforceable appeals.
Set funded delivery milestones using documented losses, urgent needs and fiscal evidence; disclose allocation reasons and protect outstanding obligations.
Create independent oversight with diverse survivor participation, conflict disclosures, audit powers and authority to remedy exclusion or diversion.
Keep acknowledgement, criminal and civil accountability, material delivery and prevention separately assessable.
Review waiting times, delivery, exclusion, unmet needs and safeguard effectiveness at published intervals; preserve criticism and revise the package when evidence warrants.
